title: AI, ML and Mathematics Foundations
objectives: Frame AI tasks using observations, outputs and measurable outcomes.
Use Python arrays, vectors, matrices and derivatives to express simple learning computations.
Connect probability, loss functions and optimization to a tested numerical example.

concepts.title: AI vs ML vs Deep Learning vs Generative AI

title: Deep Learning and Neural Networks
objectives: Trace a neural network through forward computation and gradient-based parameter updates.
Compare activation functions, regularization and optimizer choices using controlled experiments.
Select and explain basic convolutional and recurrent architectures for their intended data structures.

title: NLP and Language Processing
objectives: Build lexical text representations and explain information lost during preprocessing.
Compare word, sentence and sequence representations through explicit tasks and evaluations.
Inspect subword tokenization and connect token choices to language-model inputs.

title: Transformers Architecture
objectives: Derive scaled dot-product attention and track query, key and value dimensions.
Explain transformer components, positional information and encoder/decoder responsibilities.
Compare BERT, GPT and T5 objectives without conflating training with inference.

title: Large Language Models
objectives: Distinguish model parameters, tokens, context and training stages.
Experiment with decoding settings and explain their limits and failure modes.
Evaluate model selection, context use and caching against a defined application task.

title: Prompt Engineering
objectives: Design explicit instructions and demonstrations with measurable acceptance criteria.
Version prompts and validate structured outputs against an application contract.
Evaluate context choices, prompt regressions and adversarial input handling.

title: LLM APIs and Model Ecosystem
objectives: Integrate documented remote and local model interfaces with server-held credentials.
Handle streaming, structured responses and tool proposals with explicit validation.
Measure and limit token usage, retries, request rates and serving costs.

title: Embeddings and Vector Databases
objectives: Derive and test vector similarity functions with explicit numerical contracts.
Compare exact search with approximate indexes using recall and resource measurements.
Design versioned vector collections with metadata filters and authorization boundaries.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation
objectives: Build a document-to-answer pipeline with traceable source versions and citations.
Evaluate parsing, chunking, retrieval, reranking and context construction separately.
Compare advanced retrieval approaches against an exact, authorized baseline.

title: Fine-Tuning and Model Training
objectives: Prepare and validate instruction datasets with leakage and quality checks.
Explain full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA and quantization through their parameter and resource trade-offs.
Evaluate, version and deploy trained artifacts with reproducible configuration.

title: LangChain and LangGraph
objectives: Compose documented model, prompt, retrieval and output-validation interfaces.
Implement explicit graph state, conditional routing and checkpoint recovery.
Trace failures and enforce human-review boundaries in tool-using workflows.

title: AI Agents and Agentic AI
objectives: Separate agent observations, state, planning, tool proposals and execution authority.
Implement bounded workflows with validated tools, persistence and human escalation.
Evaluate single-agent and multi-agent systems against task, safety and resource criteria.

title: Multimodal Generative AI
objectives: Compare representations and tasks across image, audio, text and video inputs.
Explain diffusion and speech pipelines with modality-specific evaluation requirements.
Design bounded voice and multimodal applications with latency and data-handling controls.

title: LLM Evaluation and Optimization
objectives: Construct held-out evaluation sets and distinguish retrieval, generation and system metrics.
Validate judge-based assessments against explicit rubrics and human review.
Measure caching, batching, latency and token-cost changes without hiding quality regressions.

title: AI Security and Responsible AI
objectives: Identify direct and indirect prompt-injection paths through an application threat model.
Enforce permissions, sensitive-data controls and validated tool execution outside model instructions.
Evaluate safety and fairness using explicit cases, limitations and response policies.

title: Production AI and MLOps
objectives: Build authenticated asynchronous AI services with transactional storage and bounded work.
Package and deploy reproducible services with configuration and credential separation.
Trace failures, monitor application outcomes and validate scaling and rollback behavior.

title: Advanced AI Research
objectives: Read research claims in terms of assumptions, baselines, methods and reproducible evidence.
Compare compression, efficient inference and distributed-compute trade-offs using measurements.
Train and evaluate a small language-model experiment without overstating its capabilities.

title: Industry Projects and Portfolio
objectives: Deliver project artifacts with explicit user problems, testable requirements and source documentation.
Evaluate retrieval, tool use, multilingual and voice features under realistic failure conditions.
Defend capstone architecture, security boundaries, operational cost and measured outcomes.
